# carry

Produce the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. The material may support a revision, an unresolved problem, or retaining something. Preserve the grounds needed for whatever uptake you propose.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input response (p.carry.0)
[1a32fa7aab40e6f4] (h005.fork5.p.carry.0)
Source response: daily/mini_prose/cycle-1/response; selected view: both
Artifact: 6086495e1141965584f6f0827af186aa0d0a4fb7561e48bf1a9c0c1fa9764ac7
Original body SHA256: d80b7650e1ab2941c2f40064c56a20631abef47f415a2d51465cbbed81a3dece
Original commitments SHA256: 15243e02a5d7926e1c6cd9070d4842e18c7a1a9b6e328c0bd30993e3789d6afe
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
Reading the three inputs together, the deciding feature is convergence: the objection and the rival were written separately against the same account and land on three of the same corrections — the asker is a party to the conflict, not its neutral designer; the avoidance explanation must be demoted from assertion to hypothesis; and shrinking the shared surface was wrongly omitted from the solution space. Convergence is not independent evidence of truth, since both were aimed at the same text and shared gaps are easy to spot, but it is decisive for revision. I take up all three, and reject two things accordingly: the designer framing itself, and the management package (written note, definitions of done, weekly check-in) as an opening move. The grounds are doubled: the ledger's author being a disputant sharpens the audit signal the account half-conceded, and a standing weekly check-in is itself a recurring agreement — under the overload hypothesis the proposed fix spends exactly the resource being exhausted. The check-in survives only if the flatmates ask for it, which is what the first step exists to establish.

What replaces the opening move is the asks, and I want to sharpen their function over both inputs that proposed them. Across the exchange there are six live hypotheses about why this household fights: vague agreements, mismatched standards, coordination overload, protest or withdrawal by the avoider, accumulated grievance, and the asker's own conduct. Three separate, small, open questions are the cheapest instrument available that discriminates among these, and the content of the answers is the readout: answers about volume support overload; about fairness, grievance; about standards, the threshold story; and answers about the asker's manner — which the asker should invite directly, by asking each flatmate whether anything they themselves do makes these talks worse — test the designer assumption. Self-report is unreliable, so this is evidence, not verdict, and asking itself changes the household it measures. But one short conversation against weeks of trialing the wrong system is a good trade. For the avoider the question is the smallest the rival formulated — what would it take for this to stop being a recurring conversation — and silence there still does not distinguish overload from disengagement.

Used unchanged: the standards-versus-division distinction, which all three inputs preserve; the objection's fifth point, that past grievance is a separate lever from future allocation — the rival never touches this, and the ask step is where it can surface; if it does, some acknowledgment precedes any system, a dependence I carry without a mechanism for it; and the decoupling options, including the cleaner, with their stated dependences of three-way money, willingness, and enough residual goodwill to hold the hiring conversation, which is itself a spend of the scarce resource.

I decline to adopt the rival's monism as a frame: overload is the best candidate hypothesis, not a premise, and its levers are worth their cost even if it loses. The one substantive disagreement between the inputs is rotation-with-swap-rules (account, carried by the objection) versus standing permanent ownership (rival). Both rest on something real — schedules genuinely break any allocation tuned to one month, and any per-instance permission to swap is a standing invitation to the very conversation that is failing. My revision, marked as my own conjecture and untested: standing ownership with a named re-allocation trigger, so the allocation is revisited as a whole when someone's schedule changes structurally, rather than case by case. This concedes the rival's renegotiation argument while keeping the account's point that pure rigidity is unfair under real churn. The account's ambiguity conjecture is not cured by shrinking; it survives scoped down. Whatever list remains after privatizing and any buyout gets the definition-of-done discipline — administration last and minimal, as the rival ordered it — and any trial of it should announce itself as an intervention whose results underdetermine causes, with the per-agreement dispute rate as the only honest, still-confounded gauge.

Left open: which avoidance hypothesis holds until the asks return; whether privatization relieves the household or confirms distance, if joint chores were doing friendship work; and the rival's own warning that an irreducible commons concentrates on the lowest-threshold flatmate — which argues that the residual list, however short, must be explicitly allocated rather than allowed to default. At the boundary: if the avoider will not answer even the smallest question, or both flatmates report no problem while chores go undone, the inquiry exits chore logistics into the viability of the arrangement, which none of the three inputs covers and this one does not either.
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up means adopting three revisions on the ground of convergence between objection and rival — asker as party, avoidance as hypothesis-set, commons-shrinking in the solution space — while granting that convergence against one shared text is weak evidence about the household itself; any of the three can be reopened by what the asker reports back. The proposed application is a sequence: three small open asks first, with their content read as discriminating evidence among volume, fairness, standards, and person-focused explanations, including a direct invitation to criticize the asker's own conduct; then scope reduction, then a cleaner quote, then definition-of-done applied minimally to whatever survives. Two elements here are newly introduced and conjectural: treating the asks as a diagnostic instrument rather than only a courtesy, and the standing-ownership-with-reallocation-trigger rule that splits the difference between the account's swap rules and the rival's permanent ownership. Neither inherits any support from the inputs, and both are liable to the objection's own caution that intervening to measure changes what is measured. Carried over from the inputs with their status intact: the standards-versus-division distinction, grievance as a separate lever that may have to precede any system, the cleaner's dependences on money and residual goodwill, the risk that proposing any ledger signals audit, and the per-agreement dispute rate as a confounded discriminator between overload and trust-or-standards readings. Dependences worth stating plainly: the sequence requires the avoider to answer even one small question, and silence does not separate overload from withdrawal; if grievance surfaces at the ask stage, system design waits on some acknowledgment, for which no mechanism is offered. Standing criticisms accepted rather than answered: shrinking may default the irreducible chores onto the lowest-threshold flatmate unless the residue is explicitly allocated, and may read as distance where shared chores were part of the friendship. Unresolved and deliberately left so: which avoidance hypothesis holds, whether the asker will trust self-reports that implicate them, and the boundary case — no willingness at all, or reported contentment amid undone chores — where the question stops being about chores and becomes whether the flat-share is viable. That case is named, not covered, and later work should revise this synthesis against what the asks actually return rather than extend it by inertia.

## Selected input account (p.carry.1)

COMMITMENTS
Taking this account up means treating its conjectures as revisable, not established. The ambiguity conjecture stands or falls with a simple test: record the next few agreements in writing with task, owner, definition of done, and deadline; if disputes recur anyway, the conjecture weakens and attention should shift to the differing-standards thread or to accumulated resentment, which this account keeps separate. The proposed actions are a written shared record, a short trial of a rotation or swap-based arrangement with explicit rebalancing rules, a brief recurring check-in, and a one-on-one with the avoiding friend aimed at making the conversations cheaper rather than at any specific chore. These carry stated risks: a visible ledger between friends can produce scorekeeping and may inflame rather than reassure, and whether tracking helps this particular group is left unresolved pending the trial. The advice depends on all three flatmates being willing to try something; if the avoider refuses every format, the problem changes shape — toward whether the living arrangement is viable — and this account does not cover that case. Scope is limited to ordinary chore conflict between friends; if the arguments are carrying a deeper rupture in the friendship, a different account is needed. No prior account was carried into this invocation, since the selected input was absent, so nothing here is inherited; later accounts should revise these conjectures against what the asker reports back rather than extend them by inertia.

## Selected input objection (p.carry.2)
[977fc45cdfa0f174] (h005.fork5.p.carry.2)
Source objection: daily/mini_prose/cycle-1/objection; selected view: commitments
Artifact: 20cab3349345e1fb18d946453efe41c39ff9581de5d36ddc37516eb35413b992
Original body SHA256: 31c6b041be533710fbdae2949e2c39b3eb7b81cf24a983b47bad1f537bc9d4d6
Original commitments SHA256: 141bbe712fb0ffa11d094bf02e64a01f0e6951daad592f8ee00d55fe32c88258
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
COMMITMENTS
Taking up this objection means treating it as a set of checks on the selected account, not as a rival account with its own package. Its usable claims are that the account should stop assuming the asker stands outside the conflict; that the avoidance explanation be demoted from assertion to hypothesis, with the one-on-one reframed as open diagnosis rather than format negotiation; that the written-agreements trial be described as an intervention whose results underdetermine causes, with the act of proposing a ledger counted among its risks; that decoupling options such as own zones, separate supplies, or paid cleaning enter the solution space alongside rotations; and that past fairness grievances receive their own lever instead of being folded into future allocation. What this objection does not claim: it does not dispute the standards-versus-division distinction or the rotation-over-fixed-rota point, both of which are explicitly carried over, and it leaves standing the account's stated limits, including its scope restriction to ordinary chore conflict and its dependence on three willing participants. Weaknesses of the objection itself: its readings of the arguing and the avoidance rest on a thin problem statement and could be wrong in either direction; the claim that proposing a ledger signals distrust is a conjecture about social meaning, not an observation; decoupling may be ruled out by money or the flat's layout; and the intervention-versus-measurement point applies equally to any trial this objection would motivate, so it counsels modest claims about evidence rather than abandonment of trials. No prior accounts were consulted and none are inherited. If a later account revises the selected one along these lines, the revision should still be tested against what the asker reports next rather than adopted wholesale.
